sb_prompt: WHAT DO YOU CONSIDER THE MOST IMPORTANT BENEFITS BESIDES SALARY IN A JOB WITH A LARGE ORGANIZATION?  HOW SATISFIED ARE YOU WITH THE CURRENT BENEFITS OF YOUR JOB?
turns: Yeah, so basically, looking past the paycheck, the health stuff is huge because honestly, I had a nasty episode last year and the out-of-pocket costs were just... uh, terrifying. But the retirement plan? That feels a little vague to me, like it's there but not really enough to count on. What about you?

Yeah, that's exactly where I'm at. The health stuff, it's been a lifesaver for sure, especially since I had to take off a few weeks last spring for back surgery. But the retirement? Honestly, it just feels like it's not enough to really count on, like you said. It's just sort of... there.
Yeah, exactly. It feels like the company is just putting it there so we can't complain, but they never actually tell you what you'll get if you stay long enough.

Right? It's just this little bucket they throw in the corner and hope it's enough when you're seventy, but you never really know how much's in there. And then the other stuff, like the gym membership or the extra dental? That's where I think they're doing okay. I actually really like the free tuition credits for my kids' college; that's something they've got down. But yeah, the retirement plan... honestly, I never looked it over past the first page. I just assumed I'd have to save up for that myself.

Yeah, free tuition is actually one of the only things that really sticks with me, probably because I went to community college and know how steep those books get. But honestly? I kind of half-believe it's just a trap to make us stay longer. Do you feel like you actually use those credits, or do you just think it's nice on paper?

I actually use them, I mean I'm not here myself but my daughter went to school last year and used the discount and it was pretty huge, like it basically paid for her textbooks so that was really helpful.
That's good to hear though, because I actually kind of wish my kid could use it too, but we don't have the kids' stuff set up yet.

Yeah, I guess it's just weird that I never saw it until now, but now that I know, it feels like a real perk. And about the kids stuff, well, I've got two, so I know how expensive it gets, but honestly I'm just glad we can at least cover the basics if we need to.

Yeah, I totally get that feeling of "why didn't I see this sooner," it's like it was hiding in plain sight until you needed it. And honestly, thinking about having one someday... I guess the free tuition would be huge if I ever decide to try again, saves me from needing to go into massive debt for books and everything.

Yeah, exactly, I'm just glad they finally added those mental health days because honestly before that I felt terrible taking a day off for something that wasn't even an emergency.
Yeah, but it feels kind of hollow knowing that if I actually get sick or need a procedure, I still might hit those high deductibles before the insurance even kicks in.
